subtype: Approach: pushing it off until just before bedtime [Pitfall]
passage: At the hostel study hour, Dev told himself there was plenty of time. He played cricket in the corridor with a rolled-up sock and watched cartoons in the common room. When the 9 o'clock bell rang, he opened his science file and saw the diagram of the digestive system. It would take an hour. His stomach dropped. Tears came, and he walked to the warden's room. "Bidisha Ma'am, I have not started." Bidisha sat with him, helped him see where to begin, and stayed while he drew the first outline. Lights out came before the labels were done.

qa.q: What was Dev doing instead of homework during study hour?
qa.a: He played cricket in the corridor and watched cartoons.

qa.q: What was Dev feeling when he opened the science file at 9 o'clock?
qa.a: He felt panicked and sad. His stomach dropped, tears came, and he went to the warden for help.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Dev use another evening, and why?
qa.a: He could look at his homework first and put the longest task at the start. Then he would know how much time it really needs.

qa.q: How does Bidisha see Dev arriving at her room at that hour?
qa.a: Bidisha sees a child who is upset, not lazy, and who chose to ask for help. Bidisha sits with him while he begins.

grounding: A boy tells himself there is plenty of time, plays until 9 pm, then finds the diagram takes an hour, cries and asks an adult to help.
